The test image shows tomato leaves with multiple dark brown/gray circular lesions with darker centers and what appear to be concentric ring patterns. Some lesions are elongated along veins. This pattern is characteristic of either **Early Blight** (concentric target rings) or **Septoria Leaf Blotch** (small circular spots with dark margins).

Let me view one reference from each top candidate class.
This Early Blight reference shows severe whole-plant blight. The test image has more discrete circular spots on green leaves. Let me check Septoria Leaf Blotch.
Septoria shows tiny spots with yellowing - the test image has larger, darker spots. Need 2 more class views. Let me check Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus (ring patterns) and Bacterial_Speck (dark spots).
TSWV shows purplish bronzing - doesn't match. For my 4th view, let me check Early Blight with a closer leaf shot to confirm the concentric ring pattern.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Tomato leaves with discrete, medium-large circular/oval spots. Dark gray-brown centers with lighter surrounding halos and faint concentric ring patterns. Spots are scattered across green leaves, some elongated along veins.

- **Early Blight** (view 1): Showed whole-plant severe blight — too advanced to see individual spots. View 2 also showed severe necrosis, not characteristic target spots.

- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Small circular spots with dark borders and yellowing — test image spots are larger and have darker, more necrotic centers than Septoria.

- **TSWV**: Purple/bronze bronzing with tiny specks — clearly doesn't match.

The discrete medium-large spots with concentric ring-like dark centers and lighter halos on green tomato leaves are the hallmark of **Early Blight** (Alternaria solani). The spot morphology (target-board appearance, dark center, halo) and scattered distribution on the leaf are consistent, even though the reference images I viewed showed advanced/severe stages.
